recent_articles.title: Sebi, CBDT ease PAN rules for foreign investors after onboarding concerns - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sebi** and the **CBDT** have issued clarifications to simplify the PAN allotment process for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).  Following concerns raised by FPIs about the new PAN application forms, **CBDT** clarified that the name of the authorized signatory on the Common Application Form would suffice for representative assessee or authorized representative information. The tax department also eased address and contact-related compliance requirements, allowing FPIs to provide alternative contact information if details are unavailable.  These measures aim to ensure continued ease of onboarding for FPIs in India.

recent_articles.title: Angus Taylor says migrants are a ‘net drain’ on Australia. The numbers say the opposite is true | Australian immigration and asylum | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Angus Taylor**, leader of the Liberal party, has made claims about migrants being a "net drain" on society and claiming that Australia is missing out on benefits due to them. However, Treasury analysis shows that migrants pay more in taxes than they receive in government services over their lifetimes, generating significant fiscal benefits for Australia. **Alan Gamlen**, director of the ANU's migration hub, argues that restricting social security nets for permanent residents is not a solution to any problem and could negatively impact social cohesion and productivity.

recent_articles.title: Hindustan Copper Q4 Results: Cons PAT surges 135% YoY to Rs 444 crore, revenue jumps 58% - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hindustan Copper** announced a 184% increase in quarterly profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 156 crore for the quarter ending December 2026, driven by a 68% rise in revenue. The company incurred expenses of Rs 597 crore in the quarter under review, a significant jump from previous quarters. The financial results were announced after market hours, causing shares to close up 36.20 or 5.97% over Thursday's closing price.

recent_articles.title: Nithin Kamath flags how painful it is for NRIs to invest in India; Ashish Kacholia, Shankar Sharma react - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nithin Kamath**, CEO of Zerodha, and other investors have raised concerns about the difficulties Indian NRIs face when investing in India.  They argue that regulatory and compliance requirements create friction for NRIs, hindering their ability to invest and contribute capital to the country. **Ashish Kacholia**, a prominent investor, agrees, calling for a national objective of attracting USD 100 billion annually from NRIs. However, veteran investor **Shankar Sharma** disagrees, claiming his experience as an NRI has been smooth. This comes amid a sharp selloff by foreign investors in Indian markets, with FII capital heading away from Dalal Street due to geopolitical tensions, elevated oil prices, and a weaker rupee.

recent_articles.title: British Gas faces record £112m settlement over prepayment meter scandal | Energy industry | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **British Gas** will pay a £20 million penalty and provide up to £70 million in debt write-offs as part of the largest energy supplier settlement on record. The **Ofgem** investigation found that the company forced prepayment meters (PPMs) onto homes struggling with bills, violating consumer rights.  The regulator's action comes after a three-year investigation into the practice, which saw other major suppliers also face scrutiny for similar actions.  **Centrica**, the parent company of **British Gas**, acknowledged wrongdoing and has implemented changes to prevent future incidents.

recent_articles.title: UAE to complete second oil pipeline bypassing strait of Hormuz by 2027 | Oil | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The United Arab Emirates (UAE)** announced plans to complete a new oil pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz by 2027. The project aims to secure its crude exports against potential disruptions from ongoing tensions in the region, particularly following the blockade of the vital waterway.  Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Abu Dhabi's crown prince, directed the state oil company to expedite the pipeline construction. This decision comes amidst a growing rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia, with the UAE's exit from Opec signaling its intention to increase oil exports regardless of the conflict's duration.

recent_articles.title: Indian magnate Adani agrees to multi-million-dollar penalty in US court case - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Gautam Adani**, chairman of the **Adani Group**, agreed to pay a $18 million civil penalty in a US court case related to bribery allegations. The settlement, without admitting guilt, comes as US prosecutors are reportedly set to drop charges against Adani.  The case involved accusations that Adani and his subordinates misled investors about lucrative solar energy contracts obtained through bribes paid to Indian officials.

recent_articles.title: Heathrow could be forced to allow other firms to build third runway to cut costs | Heathrow airport | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Civil Aviation Authority (CAA)** has proposed changes to the regulatory model governing Heathrow Airport, including allowing other companies to design and build parts of its expansion project. The CAA's radical suggestion would allow another developer to tender for building and operating terminals at Heathrow, similar to a scheme at JFK airport in New York.  This proposal is intended to encourage competition and efficiency but could face implementation challenges. **Heathrow** argues that these changes could undermine efforts to expand the airport and create economic growth.

recent_articles.title: Indian economy: Why Modi wants Indians to buy less gold and travel less
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** urged Indians to reduce their consumption of gold, foreign travel, fuel, and other goods as the war in Iran has led to increased energy prices.  The appeal, delivered at a public event in Hyderabad on Sunday, comes amid concerns about India's economic vulnerability due to its heavy reliance on imported oil and gas. The country's forex reserves have fallen by $38 billion since the war began, and economists warn that continued pressure on the rupee could lead to further economic hardship.  **Modi** is asking Indians to voluntarily consume less in the national interest, but some economists argue that shielding consumers from price increases will worsen shortages and slow down the transition to renewable energy sources.

recent_articles.title: “Reallocate, Diversify, Reposition”: Ajay Srivastava flags rising macro risks for investors - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Srivastava**, a financial expert, warns that the recent fuel price hike will significantly impact consumer purchasing power and could lead to negative economic consequences. He advises investors to diversify their portfolios, focusing on global assets like US IT companies and gold/silver, while favoring established domestic businesses with strong promoter involvement. **Srivastava** also suggests avoiding Indian IT firms due to a lack of innovation and recommends comparing PE ratios between Indian and global companies for better valuations.  He believes the pharma sector has potential but requires careful selection, particularly export-driven businesses.
